record.context_brief: Paths with zero derivative in F-spaces
record.original_question: Let X be an F-space with no nontrivial continuous linear functionals, and let x_1 be any element of X. Must there exist a continuously differentiable path x:[0,1] -> X with x(0)=0, x(1)=x_1, and vanishing derivative x'(t)=0 for all t?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 17. - Let X be an F-space without nontrivial linear continuous func-tional. Let x-€ X . Does a function x(t) with vanishing derivative such that x(o) = 0 and x(l) = x exist ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an $F$-space, i.e., a topological vector space whose topology is induced by a complete translation-invariant metric. Assume that $X$ admits no nontrivial continuous linear functional, so that $X^* = \{0\}$. A path $x:[0,1]\to X$ is said to be continuously differentiable with derivative $x'(t)$ at $t\in[0,1]$ if the limit
$$x'(t) = \lim_{h\to 0}\frac{x(t+h)-x(t)}{h}$$
exists in $X$ for every $t\in[0,1]$ and depends continuously on $t$.

Question: For every $x_1\in X$, does there exist a continuously differentiable path $x:[0,1]\to X$ satisfying
$$x(0)=0,\qquad x(1)=x_1,\qquad x'(t)=0\ \text{for all } t\in[0,1]?$$
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches on this question (Rolewicz's Problem 17 concerning paths with vanishing derivative in F-spaces having trivial dual) did not return a definitive source confirming a complete solution or current open status. While related affirmative results are known for specific examples such as $L_p(0,1)$ with $0<p<1$, no authoritative source was located settling the general F-space case.

status_evidence.title: A topological vector space with no non trivial continuous linear form
status_evidence.snippet: Lp-spaces (for 0 < p < 1) are topological vector spaces on which there exists no continuous non-trivial linear form.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of F-spaces with trivial dual (the setting of the problem) is well documented, but no source found settling the path-with-zero-derivative question in general.

status_evidence.title: Lp-SPACES FOR 0 < p < 1 (K. Conrad)
status_evidence.snippet: If (X, M, µ) is a nonatomic measure space and 0 < p < 1, then Lp(µ)* = 0.
status_evidence.claim: Nonatomic Lp with 0<p<1 provides classical examples of F-spaces with no continuous linear functionals, but the general path question is not resolved in the references found.
